payload.title: Four series: nth-term test, telescoping sum, absolute versus conditional convergence, ratio test

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: (a) Determine whether the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{n+2}{2n+1}$ converges or diverges. Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: $\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{n+2}{2n+1}=\dfrac12\ne0$, so the series diverges by the $n$th-term test.

rubric_rows.criterion: Limit of the general term equals 1/2, which is not 0
Gives the reason for the conclusion: diverges by the nth-term test

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: (b) Show that the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{n(n+3)}$ converges, and find its sum. (Hint: Write the general term as a difference of two simple fractions.)
parts.model_answer: $\dfrac{1}{n(n+3)}=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{n}-\dfrac{1}{n+3}\right)$; the partial sums telescope and the sum is $\frac{11}{18}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Partial fractions decomposition
Telescoping gives the sum (value)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: (c) Does the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{(-1)^n}{n^{1/2}}$ converge absolutely, converge conditionally, or diverge? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The terms alternate, $\dfrac{1}{n^{1/2}}$ decreases and approaches $0$, so the series converges by the Alternating Series Test. The series of absolute values $\sum\dfrac{1}{n^{1/2}}$ is a $p$-series with $p=1/2\le1$, so it diverges. The series converges conditionally.

rubric_rows.criterion: Checks the Alternating Series Test conditions: terms decrease and approach 0
Series converges by the Alternating Series Test
Absolute series is a divergent p-series, so the convergence is conditional

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: (d) Determine whether the series $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{4^n}{n!}$ converges or diverges. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{4^{n+1}/(n+1)!}{4^n/n!}=\lim\dfrac{4}{n+1}=0<1$, so the series converges by the Ratio Test.

rubric_rows.criterion: Limit of the ratio of consecutive terms equals 0
Gives the reason for the conclusion: converges by the Ratio Test since the limit is less than 1
